subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup policy should OpenClaw use when required SecretRef providers fail under a supervised gateway restart loop?
rationale: The current code intentionally fails closed on startup secrets, but repeated supervisor restarts can amplify side-effecting credential-provider calls; choosing retry, degraded startup, circuit breaking, or external-provider delegation changes security and operator recovery semantics.

options.title: Approve generic startup protection
options.body: Define a bounded, provider-agnostic startup retry or degraded-startup policy with clear diagnostics and repair access, without hardcoding 1Password-specific behavior.

options.title: Keep fail-fast plus external resolvers
options.body: Keep startup fail-fast semantics and document supervisor limits plus external caching/batching resolvers as the supported mitigation.

options.title: Narrow to provider API discussion
options.body: Track this as a broader SecretRef provider-contract/API gap before changing startup behavior or adding retry configuration.

recommendation.title: Approve generic startup protection
recommendation.body: Define a bounded, provider-agnostic startup retry or degraded-startup policy with clear diagnostics and repair access, without hardcoding 1Password-specific behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The external secrets and eager runtime activation history points to this owner as the best available decision route for SecretRef startup policy.
